newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Patten says Hong Kong faces challenging new year.
newsitem.headline: Patten says Hong Kong faces challenging new year.

text.p: In his last Lunar New Year address, Hong Kong's colonial Governor Chris Patten on Thursday wished the territory a prosperous Year of the Ox and took a nostalgic look at his time in the territory.
"We look forward from this New Year to the challenging year ahead. I think we can do so with quite a bit of confidence," Patten said in a televised address to Hong Kong's 6.3 million people.

Calling the coming year a "poignant and exciting time for everybody", Patten said it was particularly so for him and his family as he prepared to leave the territory as Britain's last governor after more than 150 years of colonial rule.

Patten's five years in the top job -- and Britain's say in the running of the territory -- will end at midnight on June 30 when Hong Kong comes under Beijing's rule as a Special Administrative Region (SAR) and shipping tycoon Tung Chee-hwa becomes its first post-colonial leader.

"I'll leave Hong Kong this summer, with...a good deal of nostalgia, a good deal of feeling for one of the finest places in the world, one of the greatest cities in the world, and I'm sure that Mr Tung -- when he becomes Chief Executive of the SAR -- will be committed to doing all he can to keep things that way," Patten said.

Patten will pass his successor the reins to a vibrant business hub and bustling crossroads of cultures. But Tung is already feeling the burden of some of his more controversial legacies, including widespread political reforms.

China has promised Hong Kong 50 years of autonomy but has fuelled concern by recommending that a string of laws be repealed after the handover -- including parts of the Bill of Rights and two laws that allow political demonstrations and the free association of groups such as political parties.
Beijing also plans to scrap Hong Kong's elected legislature.
